overview.text:
Srinagar, at about 1,585 m, is the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, spread around Dal Lake. Shikaras glide past carved wooden houseboats, and on the slopes above the lake the Mughal gardens — Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh and Chashme Shahi — step down in terraces of lawns, fountains and water channels. The old city has the wooden Jamia Masjid, the papier-mâché-decorated Khanqah-e-Moula and bazaars full of pashmina and handicrafts.

Since June 2025 the railway has linked the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India, and Srinagar's airport has flights from Delhi, Mumbai and Jammu. Before planning a visit, check current travel advice: as of October 2026 the UK government advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir.

how_to_reach.text: Srinagar International Airport has regular flights to Delhi, Mumbai, Jammu and other cities. Since June 2025 the Jammu–Baramulla railway has run through to Srinagar, cutting Jammu–Srinagar travel time to about 3 hours.

overview.text: Dal Lake covers about 18 sq km at the heart of Srinagar. Carved wooden houseboats — a legacy of British visitors, who were not allowed to own land — line its shores, and shikaras with heart-shaped paddles ferry visitors across the water and through channels to Nagin Lake. At dawn, a floating vegetable market gathers near Nehru Park. The floating gardens bloom with lotus in July and August, and in the coldest winters the lake can freeze. There is even a floating post office on a houseboat, and the white marble Hazratbal shrine stands on the shore.

places.name: Shalimar Bagh
places.summary: The largest Mughal garden in Kashmir, laid out by Jahangir in 1619.
places.seoDescription: Visit Shalimar Bagh in Srinagar: Jahangir's 1619 Mughal garden, its three terraces, the Shah Nahar channel, chinar trees and nearby Nishat Bagh.

images.alt: A stone cascade and fountain in the central channel of Shalimar Bagh under chinar trees
images.caption: Shalimar Bagh

overview.text: Shalimar Bagh is the largest Mughal garden in Kashmir. The emperor Jahangir laid it out in 1619, and Shah Jahan had it extended in 1630. Its 12.4 hectares descend in three terraces along a single central channel, the Shah Nahar, adapting the Persian four-part garden to the hillside. On the lowest terrace, the Diwan-e-Aam has a small black marble throne set over a waterfall. Huge chinar trees shade the lawns. Jahangir named the garden Farah Baksh, 'the delightful'; Shah Jahan's extension was called Faiz Baksh, 'the bountiful'.

items.body: The Shah Nahar channel and its cascades.

overview.text: Pari Mahal, the 'Palace of Fairies', is a terraced garden-palace on the Zabarwan range built by Dara Shikoh, Shah Jahan's eldest son, and also used for the study of astrology and astronomy. overview.text:
Gulmarg lies in a cup-shaped valley of the Pir Panjal at 2,650 m, about 56 km from Srinagar; legend says Sultan Yousuf Shah named this 'meadow of flowers' in the 16th century. In winter it is India's best-known ski resort, with snowboarding, heli-skiing and tobogganing. In summer the meadows fill with wildflowers, and the golf course is among the highest anywhere.

The two-stage Gulmarg Gondola climbs from the resort to Kongdoori and on to about 3,980 m on Apharwat; the stages take roughly 9 and 12 minutes. Check current travel advice first: as of October 2026 the UK government advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir, including Gulmarg.

overview.text:
Pahalgam — the 'village of shepherds' — sits at about 2,200 m on the Lidder River and is the gateway to the Amarnath cave pilgrimage. Its meadows, pine forests, and apple and walnut orchards surround a river known for trout fishing and rafting, and nearby Betaab Valley is famous from Bollywood. It is also a trekking base, including the hard trek to the Kolahoi Glacier. Shrines include the Mamleshwar Temple and the Aishmuqam Sufi shrine.

On 22 April 2025, militants killed 26 civilians, most of them tourists, near Pahalgam. As of October 2026 the UK government advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir, including Pahalgam — check current advice before planning a visit.
